question.problem:
Evaluate the mixed integral

$$
{∬}_{D}[{\int }_{0}^{y{z}^{2}}\frac{12}{z}\,\text{d}x]\text{d}A
$$

where the region $D$ in the $yz$-plane is given by

$$
D=\{(y,z)\,:\,1\le y\le 2,\,1\le z\le \sqrt{2y}\}.
$$
question.worked_solution:
First, we evaluate the inner integral with respect to $x,$ treating $y$ and $z$ as constants:

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{D}[{\int }_{0}^{y{z}^{2}}\frac{12}{z}\,\text{d}x]\text{d}A & ={∬}_{D}\frac{12}{z}[x]_{x=0}^{x=y{z}^{2}}\,\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}\frac{12}{z}(y{z}^{2}-0)\,\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}12yz\,\text{d}A\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we evaluate the double integral:

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{D}12yz\,\text{d}A & ={\int }_{1}^{2}{\int }_{1}^{\sqrt{2y}}12yz\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{1}^{2}[6y{z}^{2}]_{z=1}^{z=\sqrt{2y}}\,\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{1}^{2}6y((\sqrt{2y})^{2}-1)\,\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{1}^{2}6y(2y-1)\,\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{1}^{2}12{y}^{2}-6y\,\text{d}y \\  & ={[4{y}^{3}-3{y}^{2}]}_{y=1}^{y=2} \\  & =4(8-1)-3(4-1) \\  & =19\end{aligned}
$$
